- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–15% if recent sentiment is negative.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then allow gradual decline.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; add 1–3 days of downward correction after sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven markets; add 2–5% buffer if sentiment volatility >0.5 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overestimate upward bias; apply 3–7% downward adjustment unless confirmed breakout.
